_note: DROP PODS, 3 of 3. The fight, then the care: clear the pod crews, then treat the three people they hurt. MB87a's triage on the back of a drop, so the fight carries a feeling (the gap in the 11-02 feelings chart: combat closes on 'done').
THE PLAYER'S PART: the fight, then the spend: clear the drop, then one med pack each for three people, in the foreman's order.

REWORKED 2026-11-10 on OT-9A: the wounded are people in talks now, in a fixed order (talks do not group), placed away from RECenterLocRef where the pods land; wounded people sit in CaptiveFaction, so the crews leave them be (Eliza's manual). The details kept: the stitches counted to four, the ribs who asks after the others, the ankle who wants to know if you saw the pods.
Ruth Pargeter's register on the speaker: level, counting, not warm; the care is in the accuracy. Voice borrowed until his ear casts it. No names, places, factions or currency in any voiced line.

place._theme: A quiet site under a pod raid, open sky at the centre.

prose.name: Rescue: After the Drop at the <Place> on <Planet>
prose.briefing: Raiders are dropping onto the <Place> by pod for the second time this week. Three of its people were hurt in the last drop, and nobody can reach them until the pods are dealt with.
prose.card: Settlement Contract. Clear a drop pod raid at the <Place> on <Planet>, then treat the wounded. Bring med packs. Payment on contract completion.

broadcast: They're dropping on us again, second time this week. Three of ours are still down from the last one. Crews first, please, and then the three.
_speech: Ruth's counts: the second time, the three. No line names how anyone feels.

beats._at: The open middle of the site, for the pods' sky.
beats.objective: Clear the pod crews at the <Place>
beats.journal: I cleared the pod crews at the <Place>. Now the three hurt in the last drop: the shoulder first, then the young one, then the ribs.
say: That's the drop dealt with. Three of ours, three med packs. The shoulder first, she's lost the most. Then the young one, then the ribs.

beats.objective: Treat the settler with the shoulder wound

_bio.from: the site's own, here for both drops (her lines)
_bio.why_there: a stray round caught her on the way down (her lines)
_bio.wants: it to be not as bad as it looks, and to stop counting (her lines)

greeting: One of their rounds caught my shoulder on the way down. It's not deep. I've been telling myself it's not deep.

exchanges.prompt: Let me see it. I've a med pack.
reply: One. Two. Three. Four. I've lost count, and I'm not starting again, so tell me that's done.

exchanges.prompt: Were you here for the first drop?
reply: Both of them. The first one I didn't see coming. This one I hid from.

beats.journal: I stitched a gash across one settler's shoulder. Next, the young one with the ankle.

beats.objective: Treat the settler with the twisted ankle

person.name: Jory Marsh
hellos: Did you see them come down? Did you?

_bio.from: the youngest on the site (Hollis's 'the young one')
_bio.why_there: dived clear of a pod and landed badly (his lines)
_bio.wants: someone to have seen the pods come down too (his lines)

greeting: I dived clear and my ankle didn't come with me. They come in like falling stars, only they open.

exchanges.prompt: Foot up. This will take the swelling down.
reply: That's better. I'm telling everyone you came down out of the sky as well. You didn't, but that's how I'm telling it.
After. Not while it was happening. Is that strange?

beats.journal: I strapped the ankle of a settler who sprained it diving clear. Last, the one with the ribs.

beats.objective: Treat the settler with cracked ribs

_bio.from: keeps the count of who still lives here (his lines)
_bio.why_there: thrown down when a pod landed close (his lines)
_bio.wants: the others seen to before him, and the count kept (his lines)

greeting: You've seen to her? And the young one? Then I'm last, which is right. I'm only sore.

exchanges.prompt: You're more than sore. Hold still.
reply: Ribs. I heard them go when I hit the ground. That's easier. Three down, three treated.

exchanges.prompt: How many of you live here?
reply: Fewer than last month. People leave after the first drop.

beats.journal: Pods came down on the <Place> again. I cleared the crews and treated the three hurt in the drop before.
